items.title: Josh Hart Says He's 'Not In A Good Headspace' After Knicks' Loss To Pacers
items.summary: The New York Knicks' early-season frustrations surfaced Friday when Josh Hart said he is "not in a good headspace." Hart went scoreless in a 106-104 loss to the Indiana Pacers that dropped New York to 6-6. Hart said the problem is mental. "Just have to be better," said Hart. "Have to be better mentally. I just gotta get my mental right." Hart missed all four of his shots in his second game back from a weeklong absence for ankle soreness and an illness. It was Hart's sixth straight game with fewer than 10 points. Mike Brown kept him on the bench for the entire fourth quarter. Hart is shooting 36 percent from the field and he said he was unsure how to fix his approach. "Wish I could tell you," said Hart. "Don't know. ... I gotta figure out how to improve that and improve my play." Hart said the ankle injury began in training camp. He also strained a calf in September, which kept him off the court for three weeks before the preseason. New York's other starting wings have also struggled. Mikal Bridges entered the night shooting 33 percent but scored 18 points on 8-of-12 shooting. OG Anunoby had 11 points on 4-of-13 shooting and is converting 58 percent at the rim, down from his 70 percent career mark. All three wings are shooting under 40 percent from the field. Every Knicks loss has come by single digits. Anunoby said the team needs to improve across the board. "It's early," said Anunoby. "We're not where we wanna be, but it's November. Everything needs to be better."

items.title: Mike Brown Says Mikal Bridges Remains Knicks' Starter Despite Shrinking Minutes
items.summary: Mikal Bridges is playing a career-low 24.4 minutes per game, but New York Knicks coach Mike Brown is not ready to remove him from the starting lineup. Brown said Wednesday that it is too early in the season for a "panic decision." Brown addressed Bridges' role after the 115-107 loss to the Cleveland Cavaliers. Bridges played 17 minutes and scored two points. "Mikal is a starter," said Brown. "It's not a question of that. He, like a lot of players, has had their good moments and not-so-good moments. Mikal has a proven track record of playing at a pretty high level as a starter in this league. So, for me to make a panic decision and change it right now, with 10 games in or whatever we are, I'm not feeling it." Brown pulled Bridges 3:54 into the third quarter Wednesday in favor of Landry Shamet. Bridges was not in foul trouble before the decision. Bridges has played under 23 minutes in six games this season, including four games in the teens. He has appeared in the fourth quarter in only six games. Bridges is shooting 32.9 percent from the field and 26.5 percent from 3-point range. Bridges has led the NBA in minutes played in three seasons and has a 649-game streak of games played. Only five players logged more total minutes than Bridges last season. Shamet is shooting 42.1 percent from 3-point range. Brown has called him the team's best pick-and-roll defender. The Knicks' starting lineup of Jalen Brunson, Bridges, Josh Hart, OG Anunoby and Karl-Anthony Towns has a minus-9.6 net rating in more than 100 minutes, per Databallr. New York is 6-5 after winning the championship last season. Bridges signed a four-year, $150 million contract extension with the Knicks during the 2025 offseason that runs until 2029-30 with a player option for that season.
